title: Scoliosis brace
what: The brace is a rigid corset made to fit your child's body. It supports the spine while your child grows and stops the curve from getting worse.
why: Usually for children and teens whose scoliosis is clearly getting worse while they grow.
duration: making the brace usually takes several visits; the brace is worn for months or years
tell_doctor: When you noticed the curve and how it has changed
For girls, whether periods have started. This matters for judging growth
What your child does: sports, school

prepare.title: X-rays
prepare.text: Bring the spine X-ray. The doctor decides which brace is needed from it.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A thin, close-fitting seamless T-shirt, worn under the brace.

prepare.title: Talk
prepare.text: Talk with your child beforehand: the brace is treatment, not a punishment.

steps: The specialist examines the back and takes measurements or a scan of the torso
The brace is made from them
At the fitting it is adjusted so it does not press
You are shown how to put it on and take it off
After some time an X-ray is taken in the brace
feel: At first the brace is tight and unfamiliar, and deep breaths are harder
It can be hot and hard to sleep in for the first weeks
After a few weeks most children get used to it
after: Wear the brace for as many hours as the doctor said. The result depends on it
Check the skin under the brace every day
Keep up the exercise therapy. The brace does not replace it
See the doctor regularly. The brace is changed as your child grows
red_flags: Redness, sores or blisters from the brace that do not go away
Severe back pain or numb legs
The brace is clearly too small

faq.q: How many hours a day should the brace be worn?
faq.a: Usually many hours a day, sometimes almost around the clock. The doctor will set the exact schedule.
Often yes, and the brace is taken off for that time. The doctor will say which sports are fine.

reminders.text: Brace fitting tomorrow. Bring the X-rays and a thin seamless T-shirt.
